chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Zhihar is of two types: one is for which expiation is due before consummation, and the other is after consummation. The one that requires expiation before consummation is the one who says, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and does not add, 'If I come close to you, so and so.' And the one that requires expiation after consummation is the one who says, 'You are to me like the back of my mother, if I come close to you.'

key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Zhihar, a form of verbal divorce in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in expiation for Zhihar before and after marital consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal condition for expiation (*kaffarah*) in *Zhihar*, distinguishing between cases where consummation (*muwaqah*) has or has not occurred. It highlights the specific linguistic formulations that trigger immediate versus deferred expiation, reflecting the juristic precision of Shia fiqh in handling marital vows. This ruling ensures that the husband's obligation is calibrated to the actual status of the marital bond at the time of pronouncement.
